interest: This file provides a valuable administrative window into how the U.S. State Department monitored and categorized Japan's industrial development and economic policies throughout the 1930s, tracing the shift from industrial rationalization to wartime mobilization. Although the physical file contains only docket index sheets, the detailed entries and cross-references document how American diplomats and consular officers tracked structural mergers, private research from the Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau, local labor conditions in Nagoya, and the critical accumulation of naval stores and munitions in the Nagasaki Consular District. It demonstrates the State Department's central indexing practices and highlights the intersection of industrial reporting with naval intelligence and political-military forecasting prior to World War II.
keywords: Nagoya Chamber of Commerce and Industry
overview: This file consists of the Department of State's docket sheets (List of Papers, Form 10-46) for decimal file 894.60, 'Japan, Industrial Matters,' covering entries from April 1930 through July 1938. The file catalogs incoming diplomatic despatches, consular reports, and departmental memoranda concerning Japan's industrial structure, economic conditions, and mobilization efforts. Key entries record reports by American diplomats including Special Ambassador William R. Castle, Jr., Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, Consul General Arthur Garrels, and consular officers in Nagoya and Nagasaki, addressing topics such as the rationalization and merger of industries, Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau annual reviews, Nagoya labor conditions, and nationalist trends in Japanese industry. Several entries function as cross-references routing substantive reports to other decimal files, notably regarding naval matters, political forecasts, financial statistics, and the development of munitions industries and naval stores in the Nagasaki Consular District for national defense.

subfiles.summary: This two-page List of Papers (Form 10-46) indexes diplomatic despatches, consular reports, and memoranda received by the Department of State under decimal file 894.60 between April 1930 and July 1938. It details reports on Japanese industrial rationalization, economic surveys by the Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau, Nagoya labor and industrial conditions, and nationalist trends in industry. The docket sheet also records cross-references routing related documents to other classifications concerning political-economic history, general financial statistics, and munitions manufacturing and naval store accumulation in the Nagasaki Consular District.
